bib.title: One Embedder, Any Task: Instruction-Finetuned Text Embeddings

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Su, Shi, Kasai, Wang, Hu, Ostendorf, Yih, Smith, Zettlemoyer, Yu. "One Embedder, Any Task: Instruction-Finetuned Text Embeddings". Findings of ACL 2023, pp. 1102–1121.

COVERAGE: All 20 of 20 PDF pages, 73,923 of 73,923 chars. That covers the body, limitations, Appendix A–D, Tables 4–10 and the checklist. I skimmed the references. Extraction was clean.

CLAIMS
1. One 335M model beats the previous best, a 4.8B model, on average.
   number: 58.4 vs 56.5 (70-dataset average); the paper reports this as +3.4%; MTEB-56 average 61.6 vs 59.5
   setup: INSTRUCTOR is GTR-Large (T5-based) fine-tuned on MEDI. The baseline is Sent-T5-XXL. 70 datasets in 9 categories (56 MTEB, 3 Billboard, 11 prompt retrieval); 66 of them unseen in training.
   quote: "compared to the previous state-of-the-art model, Sent-T5-XXL (58.4 vs. 56.5 on average), despite the fact that INSTRUCTOR has one order of magnitude fewer parameters (335M vs. 4.8B)" (p.5, §3.1)
2. Model sizes. Instruction fine-tuning adds +5.9% over the same-size GTR at both 335M and 1.5B. XL scores 58.8.
   number: Base 0.1B, Large 335M, XL 1.5B; +5.9%; "3.4% and 4.1%" over Sent-T5-XXL
   quote: "Compared to GTR(335M/1.5B), from which INSTRUCTOR (335M/1.5B) is initialized, instruction finetuninig enhances the performance by 5.9%." (p.5, Table 2 caption)
   The largest per-category gains at 335M: "text evaluation (18.3%), classification (10.1%), and clustering tasks (8.9%)". Retrieval gains only +0.4.
3. Without instructions, fine-tuning on mixed symmetric and asymmetric data hurts. With instructions, the gains from the two kinds of data add up.
   number: none (Fig. 3 is a bar chart and the text gives no values)
   setup: MEDI split into symmetric and asymmetric groups. Each group is trained with and without instructions. Note: this is a training-time ablation.
   quote: "INSTRUCTOR suffers if finetuned without task instructions on the combination of both types of data (entire MEDI)" (p.6, §4.1)
4. Robustness to paraphrase depends on the 300 Super-NI datasets.
   number: five paraphrases per eval dataset. The best-to-worst gap is shown only in Fig. 4, with no values.
   setup: The paraphrases "follow the unified template ... with the same information and only differ in wording choices" (Table 6, p.15)
   quote: "Removing these datasets from training (w/o super-NI) substantially increases the performance gap between the best- and worst-performing instructions" (p.6–7, §4.2)
5. More detailed instructions score better. Even a bare dataset tag beats GTR.
   number: four levels: N/A, tag, simple, detailed. Fig. 5 only, no values.
   quote: "Even with trivial dataset tags, INSTRUCTOR outperforms the original GTR model" (p.7, §4.3)
6. The gains are larger on unseen domains.
   number: Geography 53.4→64.2 (+20.2%), Biology 25.7→31.3 (+21.8%), Civil 71.8→77.2 (+7.5%)
   quote: "Relative gain (%) +20.2 +21.8 +7.5" (Table 3, p.8)

Setup details: the instruction is concatenated with the text, but pooling is "mean pooling ... over the tokens in x" only, so instruction tokens are left out (p.3). The template is "REPRESENT THE (DOMAIN) TEXT TYPE FOR TASK OBJECTIVE:" (p.5). Retrieval uses different query and document instructions. Training: lr 2e-5, temperature 0.01, 20K steps, four negatives, each batch drawn from a single dataset (App. A).

LIMITS
- **Omitted instructions at inference: not tested directly.** The "w/o instruction" arms in Fig. 3 are models trained without instructions. Fig. 5's "N/A" is also not clearly an inference-only ablation. The paper never runs an instruction-trained model with no instruction, or with a wrong one, at query time.
- Paraphrase robustness covers only rewordings inside the template. Free-form or off-template instructions are untested. No gap is given as a number.
- Every ablation figure is a chart without values. There are no error bars or seed counts.
- The headline is a comparison across sizes against Sent-T5-XXL. The fair comparison is with same-size GTR.
- Some retrieval datasets get worse at 335M (Table 9): MSMARCO 42.7→39.7, NQ 55.1→50.1, HotpotQA 57.9→55.2, Touche 28.3→21.6.
- English only (p.15).
- Concessions the authors make: "only able to use four negative examples ... due to computation constraints"; no GTR-XXL run; no demonstrations in instructions (p.10, §7).
- Dated: the MTEB "SOTA" claim is as of 2022–23.

BUILDS ON: instruction fine-tuning from Zhong et al. 2021 (Findings EMNLP), Min et al. 2022, Sanh et al. 2022, Wei et al. 2022 (ICLR) and Super-NaturalInstructions (Wang et al. 2022, EMNLP). The GTR backbone and bidirectional in-batch contrastive loss follow Ni et al. 2021. Sentence-T5 is Ni et al. 2022. MTEB is Muennighoff et al. 2022. Concurrent work: task-aware retrieval with instructions, Asai et al. 2022.

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.1–2): "At execution time, INSTRUCTOR generates embeddings based on both the text input and the task instruction. The same input (e.g., Who sings the song "Love Story"?) will be encoded into different embeddings, depending on the end task". This is the best fit for the section "Instructions change what an embedding means": it shows the same text producing three different vectors in one picture. The runner-up is Fig. 3 (p.6), the with/without-instruction training ablation.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The Fig. 4 caption contradicts itself ("W/o super-NI (w/ super-NI) refers to the inclusion (exclusion)"). The figure axes extract as tick labels only, with no values. Typos in the source: "Similiarty", "finetuninig".
